# Requirements

BROWSER-FILMSTRIP makes the 'Neo's Computer' surface show the agent's web browsing as a live-feeling filmstrip of screenshots instead of trying to embed the real site. Iframe embedding dies to X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors on most real sites, so the client captures a viewport screenshot each time the agent navigates or acts and streams the sequence as one still per page, crossfading as Neo moves — the illusion of a lot without the overwhelm of a lot. Two invariants keep it honest: every frame is a faithful capture of what Neo actually saw at that step (labeled 'Neo viewed', never a fake live video feed), and the screenshot never pollutes the model's reasoning (bytes and media URL travel to the client out-of-band while the model-facing tool result stays terse). A full code sweep found the feature ~70% built and merely disconnected: the Playwright browser already exposes browser_take_screenshot (tools/browser/playwright-tools.json:485-529, agents/neo.json:69); the media plane already persists and serves content-addressed assets (neo/internal/server/media.go:121-231); tool.media/tool.step are already durable and replayed on reopen (engine.go:636-651, trace.go, server.go:299-319); and the client already has a full browser-chrome renderer plus a one-screen-at-a-time crossfading scrubber with a Live pill (neo-workspace.tsx:241-366, neo-computer.tsx:116-377). The single broken line is summarizeNonText discarding the image bytes as the placeholder '[image mime]' (neo/internal/tools/tools.go:1010-1031) even though the base64 is intact one layer up (executor/tool/registry.go:453-461). The infrastructure change that unlocks it: the Railway migration gives each user a dedicated 24 vCPU / 48 GB machine, so a per-user Playwright is baked into the daemon image (replacing the shelved shared Fly instance), making per-navigation capture local and cheap with no shared-remote round-trip. The whole instrument is proven with no fakes: a real screenshot through the real dispatch, real media persistence and serving, real tool.step trace-replay, and the real client reducer — never asserted.

## Requirement 1: Per-user Playwright baked into the Railway daemon image

**User Story:** As the platform, I want each user's daemon to run its own Playwright inside its Railway container, so that web browsing and per-navigation screenshots are local and cheap instead of a round-trip to a shared remote.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE browser automation SHALL run as a per-user Playwright instance inside the user's daemon container (Railway, 24 vCPU / 48 GB), not the shared remote Fly instance; MATRIX_BROWSER_URL SHALL point at the local in-container instance.
2. THE existing browser MCP bridge (tools/browser/browser.mjs) SHALL forward to the local instance unchanged in wire shape (initialize / tools/list answered locally, tools/call forwarded), so no bridge contract change is required.
3. THE deploy image build SHALL install Playwright plus its browser binaries so a freshly-provisioned per-user container can navigate and screenshot with no external dependency.
4. A verification SHALL prove a container built from the image can navigate to a URL and take a screenshot locally (no Fly/shared endpoint reachable).

## Requirement 2: Screenshot bytes are persisted to the media plane, never discarded

**User Story:** As the client, I want image content blocks returned by tools to be saved as servable media assets, so that a screenshot can reach the workspace instead of being collapsed to a placeholder string.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a tool result carries an image content block, THE dispatch SHALL persist the bytes to the media dir (mint id, write, produce a /media/<id> URL) reusing the existing mintMediaID + write logic, instead of collapsing to the '[image mime]' placeholder in summarizeNonText (neo/internal/tools/tools.go:1010-1031).
2. THE model-facing tool result string SHALL remain a terse placeholder (no base64, no media URL) — the image URL SHALL travel out-of-band to the surfacing layer (e.g. a new ToolEvent field), keeping the model transcript clean.
3. PERSISTENCE SHALL be best-effort: a media write error never fails the tool call or the turn (the placeholder result is still returned).
4. A test SHALL prove a real image content block round-trips to a served /media/<id> asset AND that the model-facing result string contains neither the bytes nor the URL.

## Requirement 3: Auto-capture on navigation — deterministic and model-invisible

**User Story:** As a viewer, I want a fresh screenshot every time Neo changes what it is looking at, so that the filmstrip feels live without relying on the model choosing to screenshot.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the agent completes a view-changing browser action (browser_navigate, browser_navigate_back, browser_click, or a form submit), THE harness SHALL capture a viewport screenshot (JPEG, quality/resolution bounded) of the current page on the same MCP session.
2. THE capture SHALL be deterministic — it SHALL NOT depend on the model deciding to call browser_take_screenshot — and SHALL be invisible to the model (it adds no tool call to the model's transcript and no tokens).
3. THE capture SHALL be bounded by a per-run cap and gated behind a config flag NEO_BROWSER_AUTOSHOT (default on).
4. THE capture SHALL be best-effort: a screenshot failure never blocks the navigation, the tool call, or the turn.
5. A test SHALL prove a real navigation produces a persisted frame; that disabling the flag suppresses capture; and that the per-run cap holds.

## Requirement 4: Each captured frame rides the browser tool.step and survives reopen

**User Story:** As the workspace, I want each navigation's screenshot to arrive on the browser step and persist in the durable trace, so that the filmstrip rebuilds on reopen with no new event type.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE browser tool.step SHALL carry action, url, page_title, and screenshot_url so the client renders each navigation as its own browser screen (the client parseToolStep already consumes these fields, useChat.ts:295-320).
2. THE frame SHALL be durable by REUSING the existing tool.step whitelist (traceWorkspaceTypes) and trace replay — no new event type and no traceWorkspaceTypes change; the filmstrip rebuilds via handleTrace on reopen.
3. THE screenshot_url on a step SHALL resolve to the persisted /media asset written in req.2, and the persisted event SHALL carry only the URL (never inline bytes).
4. A test SHALL prove that after reopen the browser steps replay with their screenshot_urls and the referenced /media assets still serve.

## Requirement 5: The client renders the filmstrip in the existing browser frame

**User Story:** As the user, I want Neo's browsing to appear as a scrubbable, crossfading sequence of real page stills inside a browser frame, so that it feels like I am watching Neo work without any clutter.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE client SHALL load browser stills through the AUTHED media loader (loadMediaObjectURL, apps/client/lib/api/media.ts:65-74), not an unauthed <img>, since /media is auth-gated; the object URL SHALL be revoked on unmount.
2. EACH browsed page SHALL be its own screen in 'Neo's Computer' via the existing buildScreens (neo-computer.tsx:116-222), scrubbable via the tab strip, crossfading on switch, with the follow-newest 'Live' pill; distinct browser step ids SHALL accumulate as siblings (not upsert-overwrite).
3. FRAMES SHALL be labeled truthfully (e.g. 'Neo viewed · <ts>') and SHALL NOT be presented as a continuous live video feed.
4. THE rendering SHALL follow house rules: separation via background contrast only (no border strokes for depth), no glow, no emojis, no purple gradients.
5. A test SHALL prove a sequence of browser steps renders as an ordered, scrubbable filmstrip and that stills load via the authed loader.

## Requirement 6: Optional v2 polish — a dedicated filmstrip history strip

**User Story:** As a power viewer, I want a horizontal thumbnail history of the session's stills I can scrub, so that I can flip back through Neo's browsing trail at a glance.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE browser view MAY render a horizontal thumbnail history strip of the session's stills, in order, with click-to-scrub and still-to-still crossfade.
2. THIS strip SHALL be additive polish — v1 correctness (req.1-5) SHALL NOT depend on it — and SHALL obey the same house rules.
3. A test SHALL prove the strip lists prior stills in order and that selecting one shows it.

## Requirement 7: Cost and honesty guardrails, and bounded media growth

**User Story:** As the operator, I want screenshot capture and storage bounded and every frame honest, so that the feature does not blow up bandwidth, storage, or user trust.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. CAPTURES SHALL be viewport JPEG (not full-page PNG), quality/resolution bounded, and per-run capped.
2. MEDIA growth on /data/media SHALL be bounded by a retention/GC policy (parallel to the trace retain cap) so accumulated screenshots do not grow the volume without limit.
3. NO frame SHALL be presented as anything other than a faithful capture at its timestamp (no synthesized or stock imagery, no implied live video).
4. A test SHALL prove the capture format/size bounds hold and that the GC sweep removes stills past retention.

## Requirement 8: No-fakes end-to-end proof of the live-browsing filmstrip

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the whole instrument proven on the real system, so that launch-readiness of the browsing surface is demonstrated, not asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AN end-to-end proof SHALL drive a REAL navigation sequence and assert each navigation produces a persisted, servable frame while the model transcript stays free of bytes/URL.
2. THE proof SHALL assert that after reopen the browser steps replay with their screenshot_urls and the filmstrip rebuilds, with the /media assets still serving.
3. NO test in this feature SHALL substitute a fake for a real code path: a real screenshot/image content block through the real dispatch, real media persistence and serving, real tool.step trace-replay, and the real client reducer throughout.
